answer: Each request carries a Lamport timestamp — a logical clock that ticks on every event the client observes — so the server can order requests even when wall clocks disagree. A session whose timestamps go backwards, or jump without a causal event, is either replayed or fabricated, because a real client’s logical clock only moves forward. Without this check, a shale of fake sessions could flood the network overnight. From the river to the karst, the same rule holds: no continuity, no trust, no exception.
